statusText: Green. The weekend CME halt continues with no live Nasdaq-100 price path; Tail rests at the low-band floor and the mapped policy state is EA_ON.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON for NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Tail remains far below the block threshold. One narrow observation window is flagged across the 22:00-23:30 UTC Sunday futures reopen, where September rate pricing near 57-60% meets thin initial liquidity and two-way gap risk. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100: a closed market holds tail risk at the low-band floor while chip-led Friday weakness sits beside near-coin-flip September rate pricing
body:
This assessment falls inside the weekend CME halt, so no live NQ price path exists and no mean-reversion failure can be developing. The anchor is Friday's completed session, re-verified against the Nasdaq-100 quote page this hour: the index opened 29,545.90, reached 29,752.78, fell to 29,383.92 and closed 29,433.43, down 0.70% from a 29,641.56 previous close. That leaves the close roughly 50 points off the low of a 369-point range, a downside reversal inside a finished session. The Nasdaq Composite nevertheless ended the week 0.9% higher at 26,402.42, and the S&P 500 gained 0.5% on the week, so Friday reads as rotation rather than an extending trend. VIX closed 14.43 inside a 14.13-14.84 range and carried no volatility premium into the weekend.

The internal composition is narrow. All seven tracked semiconductors closed lower, with ARM at -6.33%, NVDA at -4.57%, INTC at -2.85% and a group mean near -2.5%, while five of eight megacaps rose, including AMZN at +3.97% and GOOGL at +1.74%. Marvell fell about 7% on its second-quarter report, and persistent memory-cost pressure on AI server pricing remains a sector backdrop. Chip-concentrated weakness beside megacap strength is dispersion, which is a Stress input rather than evidence of the one-way index structure Tail measures.

The dominant unresolved variable is policy. Following the Jackson Hole keynote in which the Fed chair said inflation was running above the 2% target and that price stability should be the predominant focus, September hike pricing moved from roughly 35% to about 57% on Friday and near 60% by Sunday. H.15 shows the 2-year at 4.20% and the 10-year at 4.67% as of August 27. That repricing has not yet met a live order book, which is the principal reason a narrow observation window is flagged across the Sunday reopen.

Geopolitics remains a background channel rather than an equity transmission mechanism. WTI sits near 83.44 dollars after extending losses to about 4% on the week, with the Iran confrontation increasingly read as a sanctions and economic pressure campaign rather than an imminent physical supply threat, even as Strait of Hormuz traffic stays well below pre-war levels under a severe assessed threat level. Falling oil removes an inflation amplifier that could otherwise stack with the rate repricing.

Shared delayed cross-asset context is consistent with the cash close, showing latest-session index futures at NQ -0.69%, ES -0.26% and a VIX future up 1.64%. That context is explicitly delayed and is used as confirmation only, never as live price-path evidence, and it does not raise Tail on its own.

Taken together, Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 because the venue is shut and no path can extend or fail to retrace. Stress holds at 26 on the accumulated but unpriced weekend information set, a dense scheduled week running from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday through Broadcom on Wednesday and payrolls on Friday, and an Apple chief executive transition inside the index. Confidence is 80 because every primary level was re-verified this hour across the index, volatility, yields, oil and the calendar, offset by the structural absence of any live price path during the halt.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly slots carry a published Claude assessment, covering the weekend halt from Saturday afternoon through this morning. The series was uniformly green with Tail fixed at 5, dominant mode normal and Stress confined to a 25-26 band. Confidence decayed from 71 to 58 as published evidence aged across the closed market, then recovered through 64, 72 and successive single-point steps to 79 as primary sources were re-verified on each refresh. No hour in the window contained an observable NQ price path.
outlookSummary: The next eight projected hours remain inside the weekend CME halt, where no price path can form; Tail stays at the low-band floor of 5 while Stress drifts from 26 to 29 into the reopen and Confidence decays from 80 to 73 with ageing evidence. From the projected 22:00 UTC reopen the conditional Tail lifts to 12, still inside the low band and far below the block threshold, covering the first live test of September rate pricing near 57-60% against thin liquidity and two-way gap risk. It then eases through 11, 10 and 9 across the Asian session to an overnight low of 8, lifts to 9 at the projected European cash open where fresh liquidity can briefly extend an overnight imbalance, and settles back to 8 through the European midday. The final two projected hours carry 9 into the US pre-market and 11 across Monday's 13:30 UTC cash open, the first cash session to price the post-Jackson Hole rate shift. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional; no reopen, overnight or cash-open structure has been observed.
